references.text: The Lord gives Abraham promises of blessing, which mark the beginning of the blessings Abraham experiences in his old age.
Abraham was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold—a concrete part of the Lord's blessing.
God promises Abraham protection and great reward, further emphasizing God's blessing.
God blesses Sarah and promises her a son, as part of the comprehensive blessing upon Abraham.
Abraham and Sarah were old and had advanced far in years—the same expression (בָּא בַּיָּמִים) used in 24:1.
After Abraham's obedience in the test with Isaac, God confirms His blessing and promises numerous descendants.
Abraham's servant testifies that the Lord has blessed Abraham abundantly with small livestock, large livestock, silver, gold, servants, and camels.
Joshua was old and had advanced far in years—the same Hebrew expression (בָּא בַּיָּמִים) used for Abraham.
Paul refers to the promise given to Abraham ('In you all nations shall be blessed') as part of the gospel, now also for the Gentiles.
Narrative connection: 24:1 introduces the final phase of Abraham's life, while 25:8 describes the conclusion of that same period.
Theological cause and effect: 15:6 explains the reason for the comprehensive blessing mentioned in 24:1.
Theological link: New Testament theology on faith (Gal 3:6) explains the basis of Abraham's blessed life (24:1).
Narrative connection: 21:2 explains how Abraham reached the age described in 24:1.
Theological link: 6:15 explains the process (patient waiting) that led to the fulfillment in 24:1.
Theological parallel: God's blessing and presence over a believing leader (Abraham and David).
Narrative connection: 25:7 gives the actual lifespan that confirms the description in 24:1.
Theological connection: NT theology on faith (Rom 4:3) explains the basis of Abraham's blessed life (24:1).
Theological cause and effect: 26:5 explains the reason for the comprehensive blessing mentioned in 24:1.
Theological connection: 24:1 presents Abraham as the prototype of the blessed believer, which 3:9 extends to all believers.
Narrative context: 24:1 sets the stage for 24:12 by introducing Abraham as the blessed patriarch.
Theological parallel: God's blessing and presence over a believer (Abraham and Samuel).
Narrative connection: 21:5 gives the actual age that confirms the description in 24:1.
Theological parallel: God's blessing and presence over a believer (Abraham and Samuel).
Theological parallel: Obedience and God's blessing over a believer (Abraham and Moses).
Theological connection: 7:17 explains the historical context for the fulfillment of the promise in 24:1.
Theological connection: 51:2 gives the prophetic context for the fulfillment of the promise in 24:1.
Theological connection: 18:19 explains the reason for Abraham's blessing and role in 24:1.
Theological connection: NT theology on faith (Jas 2:23) explains the basis of Abraham's blessed life (24:1).
